chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Ziyad al-Qandy, from Dorost, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
He said: The Qunut is [performed] in every prayer, in the obligatory and the optional.
ai.seo_question: Is Qunut required in all prayers according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the permissibility and recommendation of reciting Qunut in all prayers, reflecting the Shia scholarly view that it is a confirmed Sunnah rather than a strict obligation. The chain of transmission highlights the reliability of early narrators like Muhammad ibn Muslim, reinforcing the tradition's authenticity within the Usuli framework. Practically, this supports the widespread Shia practice of raising hands during the Qunut in the second rak'ah of Fajr and other prayers, emphasizing continuous supplication as an integral component of worship.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, from Ziyad Al Qindy, from Dorost, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,
‘The Qunut is to be in every Salāt, in the Obligatory and the optional’.
en.sarwar: 15. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad Ya‘qub ibn Yazid from Ziyad al-Qandiy from Durust from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “He (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
There is Qunut (supplication after recitation in second Rak‘at) in every Salah (prayer); obligatory or optional.’” (Ahadith 13-15 are best explained in the form of fatwa.)
